data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Keri was a Nereid, a sea goddess. The name is derived from the Greek word 'kera', meaning 'horn' or 'head', symbolizing strength and power. In Christianity, Keri is associated with St. Jerome, the patron saint of librarians and scholars, whose name is derived from 'keros', meaning 'wax', symbolizing the preservation and transmission of knowledge.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength, beauty, and wisdom.
data.etymology: Keri belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lovely, Beautiful One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Keri total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: In the Greek mythology, the name Keri symbolizes strength and power, associated with the sea goddess. In the Western world, the name was used as a female given name, showcasing a rich cultural heritage that tied ancient mythology to modern naming practices.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Keri is associated with St. Jerome, whose name derived from 'keros', meaning 'wax'. This symbolizes the continuity and preservation of knowledge and faith, with St. Jerome being the notable translator of the Bible into Latin, ensuring its accessibility to a wider audience. By embracing the name, an individual may reflect on the spiritual value of knowledge and its role in deepening their faith.
